Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
740 AM EDT Sat Sep 5 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 213 AM EDT Saturday...

No significant changes have been made to the forecast at this time.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 213 AM EDT Saturday...

1. A few showers today and Sunday but mainly dry through 
Tuesday.

2. A more robust system is expected towards mid-late week, 
followed by some cooler temperatures.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 213 AM EDT Saturday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: A retrograding area of low pressure system near Nova 
Scotia will bring some isolated to scattered rain showers to the 
region throughout the day. Models are showing weak moisture 
transport but steepening mid-level lapse rates from cold advection 
aloft with be able to utilize the modest moisture and produce some 
showers through the day. We don't expect any heavy rainfall with 
amounts likely peaking around a tenth of an inch. Most places, 
however, will remain dry through the day as areal coverage will not 
be overly impressive. Rain chances will diminish as we head into 
Sunday morning but an isolated shower cannot be ruled out for the 
first part of Sunday. Thereafter, deep layer ridging will become 
established across the North Country and northern New York with 
mostly clear skies, light winds, and seasonably cool temperatures 
expected on both Monday and Tuesday.

KEY MESSAGE 2: Towards the middle of next week, a deepening low 
centered well to our north will move eastward from Ontario to 
Quebec, with associated frontal boundaries bringing more widespread 
precipitation to our region, with the most widespread showers 
currently expected Wednesday night into Thursday. Although there 
will be plenty of moisture, the better dynamics will be further 
north and the nocturnal timing will limit instability so widespread 
thunderstorm activity is not expected but trends will need to be 
monitored as we get closer. Behind this system, cooler weather will 
return for the end of the week, with high temperatures on Friday 
generally in the 60s to near 70 across the region.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z SATURDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...
Through 12Z Sunday...A mix of flight conditions continue across
the region this morning, with all terminals currently
experiencing MVFR ceilings or lower. Intermittent IFR ceilings
are expected to continue for another few hours at
KSLK/KBTV/KEFK, with improvement back towards MVFR generally
between 13Z and 15Z. MVFR conditions will linger through most of
the morning, with improvement backs towards VFR generally by 
18Z to 21Z depending on the terminal. Winds will generally 
northerly at 5 to 10 knots throughout the day, with gusts up to 
20 knots possible throughout the afternoon, before trending 
light and variable towards 00Z. A few showers may develop this 
afternoon, but left mention of them out of the TAF due to low 
confidence in timing and location.

Outlook...

Sunday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Sunday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Labor Day: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Monday Night: VFR. Slight chance SHRA.
Tuesday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Tuesday Night: VFR. Chance SHRA.
Wednesday: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. Likely SHRA,
Slight chance TSRA.

&&

NY...None.
